results.title: Indian workers fill Germany's labor gaps but face hurdles and risks
results.content: The number of Indians working in Germany has grown rapidly in recent years. But many continue to face challenges in the labor market. Some also fall victim to recruitment scams, leaving them vulnerable to exploitation.

results.title: Canada: Supreme Court largely upholds Quebec secularism bill
results.content: Quebec's government passed Bill 21 to ban religious symbols for public servants, arguing it was necessary to protect its secularist society. Critics argue the bill weakens legal protections for fundamental rights.

results.title: Divisions deepen between EU member states after tense budget summit
results.content: An EU leaders summit on the bloc's seven-year budget fell apart amid divisions over how to fund Ukraine. The budget proposal also includes a 3% tax on US tech companies, in a bid for the EU to generate additional funds.

results.title: Dutch authorities seize 26 critically endangered turtles from luggage of passenger bound for Hong Kong
results.content: The tiny Vallarta mud turtle was only discovered in 2018. It's critically endangered with around 300 thought to live in the wild. Almost one tenth of that number were stashed in a traveler's luggage, bound in duct tape.

results.title: Airline Norse Atlantic files for bankruptcy, succumbing to aviation fuel costs
results.content: The low-cost airline was only founded a few years ago and had been struggling to turn a profit. The spike in aviation fuel prices caused by the war in Iran has now driven Norway's Norse Atlantic into bankruptcy.

results.title: As Gambia gears up for election, can Barrow secure a third term?
results.content: President Adama Barrow is seeking a third term as Gambians vote on December 5. The election will test the opposition's appeal and the country's progress on democratic reform.

results.title: Informer TV owner Vucicevic arrested: Has the reckoning with Serbia's pro-Vucic media machine begun?
results.content: The arrest of media owner Dragan J. Vucicevic raises questions about whether Serbia is holding the people behind the country's pro-Vucic media accountable — or whether this is another political power struggle.

results.title: Duterte's ICC trial: What is at stake for the Philippines?
results.content: Former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte faces trial in The Hague over his deadly war on drugs. The proceedings could determine the political fortunes of a powerful dynasty. Victims' families hope to see justice.

results.title: In Iran, child marriage risks complicated by war
results.content: War, poverty and disrupted schooling could put more girls in Iran at risk of child marriage, rights advocates have warned.

results.title: Albania's youth are protesting, no longer leaving the country
results.content: Youth protests against a rigid political system and corruption have shaken the government of Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama. They also show that fewer young people are willing to emigrate in search of a better future.

results.title: Saudi pop music is thriving — but for the right reasons?
results.content: As part of Vision 2030, Saudi Arabia's music scene has evolved hugely thanks to state funding and support. Local musicians and DJs are optimistic. But are they actually just helping prop up an authoritarian state?
